title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
An AI music generation system was trained on copyrighted recordings without authorization from the rights holders. The system deployed to users without securing licenses from major record labels before doing so. The training data included copyrighted works, and the system generated new music from text prompts, which users could create and share.

This shows a model built and released before addressing core legal and contractual requirements for its domain. The failure occurred upstream of deployment: the training process used protected material without permission, and the system went live serving the public while operating outside the conditions required by copyright law and industry licensing. A review of training data sources against copyright status would have caught this before launch.

It is not established whether the use of copyrighted recordings in training was intentional, inadvertent, or what specific remedies courts will order, as litigation remains ongoing.

summary:
Universal Music Group has resolved a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio by reaching licensing agreements. UMG had accused Udio of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence system, which generates original music from text prompts. The settlement includes plans for Udio to launch a new platform next year that will only use authorized and licensed music. Artists will be able to opt into the platform and receive compensation, though specific financial terms and artist details were not disclosed.

This marks Udio's first major licensing agreement with a record label and reflects ongoing tensions between the entertainment industry and AI companies. UMG, Sony Music, Warner Music Group and others had sued Udio last year, claiming it illegally trained on hits like The Temptations' "My Girl" to create similar songs. UMG's CEO stated the agreements show the company's commitment to supporting artists while embracing new technology. Additionally, UMG announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.
